validated_work_order.understanding:
Seven follow-ups on #67's narrow-viewport overflow work, all in two files. I re-checked each against the source and two of them by running the suite, and all seven hold.

(1) /approvals still overflows. .approval-actions (styles.css:394) is `display: flex` with no flex-wrap, and its input (styles.css:400) is `flex: 1` — grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0%. Shrinking cannot help: a flex item's automatic minimum size is its content-based minimum, and an <input>'s is its intrinsic width (~234px in Chromium), which nothing in the file lowers. So the row floors at 234+63+60+32 = 389px, .approval-card is a grid item in the display:grid .approval-list, the track sizes to that, and the page scrolls at 320/375/414. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the card cannot touch it: it adds soft-wrap opportunities to text, and there is no text in the row that overflows. This is #48's defect one level down from the string.

(2) The pinned selector assertion (test/web/pages.test.js:1350) is `selector.includes('.' + cls)`, a substring test over the rule's raw text. I renamed `.opportunity-row` to `.opportunity-roww` on line 386 only, leaving `.opportunity-row *` on 389: the suite stays at 62 pass / 0 fail. The renamed rule matches nothing in the page and nothing notices. The `([^{}]+)` capture at :1344 has the same hole from the other side — a CSS comment contains no braces, so prose naming a class is swallowed into the 'selector'.

(3) Finding 5's assertion is `assert.equal(wrapping.length, 1)` (test/web/pages.test.js:1346), which counts every rule in the file that mentions overflow-wrap. I appended `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` to the end of styles.css — a sensible rule that cannot override the card rule, since .page-footer is not a card — and the suite went to 61 pass / 1 fail on the message 'exactly one rule in src/web/styles.css declares overflow-wrap, so a second one cannot override it'. The property the message states is 'no later rule re-declares overflow-wrap on one of the three card selectors'.

(4) `.experiment-card *, .opportunity-row *, .approval-card *` are dead weight: overflow-wrap is an inherited property, so the three bare classes already cover every descendant.

(5) The comment above the rule is 21 lines (styles.css:364-384) in a file whose next-longest is 9, and two thirds of it is a record of rejected alternatives that already lives in the work order and the assertion messages.

(6) .tenant-name carries no wrap. The header name is `tenants.list()[0].name`, and src/api/routes.js:191 auto-creates an unknown tenant as `{ id: tenantId, name: tenantId }` — so the rendered name is the POST /v1/events body's tenant_id verbatim. .header-status is a flex row and the span's automatic minimum floors the header at the token. Latent on the seeded preview only because tenant_demo is created first.

(7) .learning-card is a fourth free-text card list outside .table-scroll that the enumeration missed. I rendered the seeded /opportunities and it does carry `class="learning-card"` twice (the seed holds two accepted learnings), so the class is on every seeded run; only a long claim needs a fixture. No rule in the stylesheet matches it.

I could not re-measure layout in this sandbox — chromium is installed but does not start here (dbus errors, no DOM from --dump-dom) — so the pixel numbers in the ticket are taken as given and the browser-visible claims are written as ACs for QA to measure on a real runner. Every layout claim above is confirmed structurally in the CSS, and findings 2 and 5 I reproduced by running the suite.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The card-name fix from #67 was expressed as an enumerated list of three class names plus a substring assertion over the stylesheet's text, so both halves are incomplete by construction: the enumeration missed a fourth free-text card list and the header, and the assertion could not tell a selector that matches a rendered element from one that matches nothing. A separate instance of the same family — a grid or flex item floored at its automatic minimum — survived at .approval-actions, one level below where #48 and #67 fixed it.
validated_work_order.approach:
One stylesheet change covering the three live layout defects, one trim of the comment, and one rewrite of the pinned stylesheet assertion so it states the property it means.

CSS, in three places:
- The wrap rule becomes four bare classes — add `.learning-card`, delete the three `*` descendants (redundant: overflow-wrap is inherited), and replace the 21-line comment with 9 lines that state the defect, the grid-floor reason and the two constraints that must survive a future edit (scoped off the tables, `anywhere` not `break-word`).
- `.tenant-name` gains `min-width: 0` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, with three comment lines saying where the text comes from.
- `.approval-actions` gains `flex-wrap: wrap`, and `.approval-actions input` gains `min-width: 0` — the declaration that actually lets the row shrink below the input's 234px intrinsic minimum. Wrap alone does nothing here: the row is 389px of min-content against ~208px of available width at a 320px viewport, so it is min-width: 0 that does the work and the wrap that keeps the two buttons reachable when even that is not enough.

Test, in test/web/pages.test.js: rewrite the pinned assertion in the every-match style its neighbours already use, with the four changes findings 2, 3 and 5 ask for — strip comments before parsing, match compound selectors rather than substrings, scope the 'no later override' check to rules that touch the four card classes instead of counting every overflow-wrap rule in the file, and cross-check the rule's class list against the classes the server actually renders. Add a `pendingApprovalRepos()` helper, because nothing in the product writes approval.requested and no test has ever rendered an approval card; without it both the new render cross-check and the /approvals layout are unverifiable here. Add two pins: the actions row (flex-wrap on the row, min-width on the input, plus a render that shows both have something to match) and the header tenant name (the wrap, plus a render of a 137-character tenant so the selector is known to match a real element).

files.change:
Replace lines 364-392 — the 21-line comment and the six-selector rule — with exactly this, and nothing else in that region changes:

/* A free-text name on an experiment, opportunity, approval or research
   observation is one unbreakable token, and one long enough token still
   scrolls the page sideways even with the floor lifted above: a grid item's
   automatic minimum is its min-content width, and .experiment-list and
   .approval-list are both display: grid, so the track sizes to the string.
   `anywhere` rather than `break-word`, which leaves intrinsic sizing alone.
   Scoped to these four lists, never to #main: a blanket wrap reaches the
   table cells and makes every wide table wrap instead of scrolling in its
   own region. No `*` descendants — overflow-wrap is inherited. */
.experiment-card,
.opportunity-row,
.approval-card,
.learning-card {
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
files.why: Findings 3 and 7. `overflow-wrap` is inherited, so the three `*` descendants state a property the bare classes already carry; `.learning-card` renders the free-text claim on /opportunities and no rule matched it.
Finding 6. The span's automatic minimum size is the token's width, and nothing in the file lowered it; the header already wraps, so the name moves to a second line rather than being cut.

files.change:
In the `.approval-actions` rule at lines 394-398, add `flex-wrap: wrap;` immediately after `display: flex;`, and put this comment immediately above the rule:

/* The card's own min-content used to be this row: it is a nowrap flex row
   holding an <input> whose automatic minimum is its ~234px intrinsic width,
   and .approval-card is a grid item, so the track floored at ~389px and the
   page overflowed at 320px. min-width: 0 below lets the input shrink, and the
   wrap keeps both buttons reachable when that is still not enough. */

Then add `min-width: 0;` as the first declaration inside the existing `.approval-actions input` rule at lines 400-407, above `flex: 1;`. Change nothing else in either rule.
files.why: Finding 1. `flex: 1` already sets flex-shrink: 1, so shrinking is not the missing piece — min-width: 0 is, because an <input>'s automatic minimum is its intrinsic width and no wrap rule can reach a form control.
Findings 2, 3 and 5, plus the renders that make the new pins non-vacuous.

risks: Deleting the three `*` descendant selectors relies on overflow-wrap being inherited, which is true today and is the same fact #67's work order leaned on. If a future rule ever declares `overflow-wrap: normal` on an intermediate child (`.score-components span`, say), that descendant stops wrapping and the bare-class rule will not catch it, because it is not the kind of mistake the pinned assertion can see. No such rule exists in the file today.

The four class names are still a hand-maintained list. The new render cross-check catches a name that matches nothing and a class dropped from the rule, but it cannot catch a fifth free-text card list that nothing renders yet — a new `<li>` carrying free text outside `.table-scroll` needs its class added by hand, exactly as `.learning-card` did not get one.

Adding the wrap to `.learning-card` also reaches the metadata span under it (tier, confidence, evidence count, learning id), so a long learning id may now break mid-token inside the card. Cosmetic and inside a card, but it is a change no measurement in the ticket covers.

`min-width: 0` on the approval reason input lets it get narrower than its 'Reason' placeholder at a 320px viewport, so the placeholder will clip while the field stays usable. Truncating the placeholder was rejected as a product-copy decision, not a layout one.

`flex-wrap: wrap` on `.approval-actions` means that at very narrow widths the Approve and Reject buttons drop onto a second line rather than beside the input. That is the intended behaviour and matches `.journal-filters`, but it is a visual change on a screen that had no rendered card in any earlier QA run, so there is no prior render to compare against.
The mutated-file checks in AC-7 are run by hand against the working tree. Restore from git between each one; leaving a mutation in place is the obvious way to fail CI on the next run.
out_of_scope: `.awaiting-list li` on /journal?state=partial: it renders a generated decision_id and a formatted date, not user free text, so it gets no wrap. If a long decision id ever appears there it is its own ticket.

The client-rendered journal drawer body, which client.js fills from GET /v1/decisions/:id. It is a fixed-width overlay, not a server-rendered card list, and nothing in this ticket's measurements covers it.

`.checklist li` and the `.kpi-*` tiles: fixed product copy and formatted numbers, not free text. A blanket wrap would let a formatted money value break mid-digit, which is why it is not taken here either.

A blanket `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `#main`, or on every `ul`/`li` inside it. It would have found `.learning-card` and `.tenant-name` by itself, and it reaches `.table-scroll` cells and the monospace KPI values, which #67 measured undoing the table fix.

Writing an `approval.requested` event from the product — a write path, an executor call or a new seed row. Nothing creates one today, so the /approvals queue is empty in a running preview and this defect is latent. Making the queue non-empty changes what a first run shows and is a product decision the ticket does not ask for; the fix here makes the CSS correct for when one does, and the new test fixture makes it reachable for QA without one.
Truncating the tenant name with an ellipsis instead of wrapping it. The name is the only identifier the operator has for the account they are in, and the header has room to wrap onto a second line.
Any visual change to the 1100px layout. Every rule touched here applies at every width; the sweep in the QA script checks that nothing moved at 1100 and 1440, but no restyling is in scope.

alternatives_considered.approach: Scope the wrap by structure instead of by class name: `#main :not(.table-scroll *) { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }`
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It finds .learning-card and .tenant-name with no enumeration to keep up to date, which is the actual root cause. But it also reaches every formatted money value and every monospace KPI number, so a long amount breaks mid-digit, and it is one edit away from re-reaching the table cells that #67 measured undoing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the three `*` descendant selectors and just add `.learning-card`
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: overflow-wrap is inherited, so the bare classes already cover every child; the descendants state the same property three more times, and they are what the new exact-compound assertion would have to pin forever. Review finding 3 measured the same result with them removed.

alternatives_considered.approach: `flex-wrap: wrap` on `.approval-actions` alone, without min-width: 0 on the input
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Wrapping the buttons does nothing while the input is floored at its ~234px intrinsic automatic minimum: the row is ~389px of min-content against ~208px of available width at a 320px viewport, and no line break is available inside a 234px-minimum item that also has to share the line. min-width: 0 is the declaration that does the work; the wrap is kept so the buttons stay reachable when even that is not enough.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the global `wrapping.length === 1` count and instead document that no other rule in the file may declare overflow-wrap
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It pins a property about the file rather than about the fix, so the first legitimate `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` — a rule that cannot override the card rule — turns CI red. Reproduced in this run: 61 pass / 1 fail. The message already states the narrower property; the assertion should be the message.

alternatives_considered.approach: Replace the stylesheet-text pin with a real layout assertion that measures scrollWidth in CI
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would be the strongest form, and the repo has no browser driver in CI and no appetite for a native-compiling dependency. The deliberate style of the three existing pins in this file is a stylesheet-text assertion cross-checked against rendered markup, and that combination catches the exact class of mistake finding 2 describes — a selector that matches nothing in the page the server actually renders.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete the pinned stylesheet test altogether, since findings 2 and 5 show it asserts the wrong things
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Those findings are defects of the assertions, not of pinning. The stylesheet is not observable from a rendered page and the browser check that would catch its regression is not in CI, so removing the pin leaves #67's fix unpinned with a green suite — the state finding 2 describes.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the /approvals overflow by hiding the reason input at narrow widths rather than shrinking it
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes what the screen offers: an operator approving a spend at 320px would lose the reason field with no way to reach it, and no acceptance criterion or UI doc asks for that.
